name: First Fork Last Camp
description: This is the final campsite at the end of First Fork Road, tucked beside the river in a quiet, remote section of the camping area. The site is best suited to one or two vehicles, though there is another larger site just up the road that can comfortably handle a group of roughly three to four vehicles and/or a small trailer. The ground is fairly level, but some minor leveling may still be needed depending on where and how you park. The site sits close to the water with limited direct sunlight because of the surrounding terrain, although solar still works well enough to maintain a modest battery setup. An outdoor wheelchair should handle the site reasonably well. Pit toilets are available at the opposite end of the camping area near the trail parking, and there is also a small hidden hose along the road that is fed by a natural spring.
sensorySummary: This is a very peaceful site overall. The river is the dominant sound, which helps mask most other noise and makes the area feel calm and predictable. The main interruption comes from fly fishers and hikers using the small trail behind the campsite, so people may occasionally pass directly through or near the site during the day. If that level of interaction is manageable, this can be a very good place for sensory recovery. The moving water is especially calming, and depending on river depth, there are larger rocks where you can sit out near the water while staying dry. Privacy is better than a roadside pullout, but it is not completely isolated because of the trail traffic.
accessSummary: The site is located at the end of First Fork Road and is suitable for standard vehicle camping. The ground is mostly level, though small adjustments or leveling blocks may be useful depending on where you park. The site itself is better for one vehicle, while the larger nearby site has enough room for several vehicles and a small trailer with a limited turnaround area. Outdoor wheelchair access is reasonable around the campsite itself, although conditions may vary depending on weather and ground moisture. Pit toilets are located elsewhere in the camping area near the trail parking rather than directly at the site.
notes: Final campsite at the end of First Fork Road.

Maximum stay 14 days.

name: Chimney Rock Pulloff

connectivity.starlinkNote: Excellent unobstructed sky view. Starlink rating is based on site geometry and clear sky exposure, not an actual Starlink test.

season.seasonalAccessNote: Access can change with snow, mud, fallen trees, and temporary Forest Service closures.

description: A small roadside vehicle pullout along Snow Ranch Road / FS 628 near Chimney Rock. The site fits one vehicle up to roughly 25 feet and offers excellent mountain and night-sky views. It is easy to access in a sedan and has strong cellular service, but it is highly exposed to passing traffic and provides essentially no daytime privacy. Traffic drops off substantially at night, making it much better suited to a quiet evening or overnight stop than an extended campsite.
sensorySummary: Daytime activity and exposure make this a poor choice for someone seeking a secluded sensory retreat. Passing vehicles and pedestrians are noticeable and the site has virtually no visual privacy. At night, conditions become significantly quieter and darker, with very little traffic and excellent stargazing.
accessSummary: Easy dirt-road access suitable for normal passenger cars. Some rocks are present and downed trees are always possible. No high clearance or four-wheel drive is normally required.
notes: Sedans regularly use the road.
A rock or two may be needed to level the vehicle.
Maximum practical vehicle length is approximately 25 feet.
The site accommodates one vehicle.
No suitable tent camping area.
Passing vehicles may create occasional dust.
Nearby house lights are faintly visible at night.
Traffic was essentially absent overnight during the observed stay.
Excellent T-Mobile and Verizon service during the visit.
Large unobstructed sky area should provide excellent Starlink visibility.
